name: aversion to loss
quote: I need to buy it now in case the price goes up.
description: A desire to avoid losing a particularly valued thing if at all possible.
perceptions: If I lose this game or asset I'll regret it forever.
results: you may avoid participating in something if there's a chance for loss.
examples: selling stocks on a short term dip

guidance.description: Loss aversion is a natural human tendency that exists to keep us from incurring losses. That being said, it is essential to know how to avoid loss aversion to prevent it from influencing our decisions, especially when there are potential gains to be made. There are two main strategies we can use to fight back against this bias: framing and putting loss into perspective.

variations.name: aversion to regret
variations.description: A desire to avoid doing something (or not doing something) that could result in a negative self-evaluation.
perceptions: If I do (or don't do) this thing, I may regret it.
I would prefer to avoid that negative feeling.
desires: desire to be seen a certain way

guidance.description: Regret aversion is when the anticipation of regret is factored into a decision, leading us to a preference that minimizes potential regret. Fear of regret can play a significant role in either motivating a person to take action or dissuading them from making a decision.

comparisons.description: FOMO is a specific kind of 'aversion to regret' that's focused on social experiences.

variations.name: aversion to change
variations.description: A desire to avoid change of some type that could possibly result in doubt, a loss, or regret.
perceptions: I understand the current state of things.
If I let them change, I may not understand it as well or it may not be as good.
Best to resist change in this area.
desires: desire to be seen a certain way

guidance.description: There are many references to help you understand and manage a fear of change. Here are some.

comparisons.description: The sensation of 'losing' is what happens after you've lost. 'Aversion to loss' is a feeling of anxiety that can arise as you predict a potential loss.

commentaries.quote: When directly compared or weighted against each other, losses look larger than gains.
Loss aversion helps produce inertia, meaning a strong desire to stick with your current holdings.
commentaries.attribution: Richard H. Thaler in 'Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness'

commentaries.quote: Letting go of attachments to material possessions, relationships, or past experiences that stifle or no longer serve us can be liberating and allow us to move forward with our lives. When we contain our 'loss aversion,' we learn to bounce back from setbacks and master the qualities for navigating life's challenges.

Loss aversion plays a significant role in cheating behavior. Players are more likely to cheat to avoid losing progress or status than to gain something new. This mirrors real-world behaviors where people are more likely to cheat on taxes to avoid owing money than to get a bigger refund.
commentaries.attribution: sobrief.com review of Jamie Madigan in 'Getting Gamers'

commentaries.quote: Behavioral and neuroscience would tell us that, on average, one dollar of loss creates twice as much pain as one dollar of gain creates happiness.
Change is never painful. Only the resistance to change is painful.
If it ain't broke, don't fix it.
